title: Expose resolved hierarchy through the server API and output schemas
description:
Serve core hierarchy resolution to external consumers: resolved fields on the HTTP graph endpoint, a published schema for the tree output, and one consistent field set across export surfaces.

## Background

Core resolves parent/children/cluster/rank in `graph/hierarchy.rs`, and `jit graph tree` emits the full `HierarchyNodeView` (`output.rs:848-866`). But `GET /graph` (`crates/server/src/routes.rs:124-163`) ships only raw edges plus labels, `export_json_full` (`visualization.rs:208-238`) emits only `resolved_parent` and `cluster` (no children/rank), and `get_output_schema_for_command` (`schema.rs:359-410`) has no `graph_tree` arm even though the types derive `JsonSchema`. External consumers therefore re-derive resolution and re-parse `type:` labels.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-1: Each node in the `GET /graph` response carries resolved parent, children, cluster, rank, and the resolved type value, all computed by core resolution in the server (no client-side derivation required).
- [hard] REQ-2: The published output schema set includes the graph-tree response shape, retrievable through the schema command.
- [hard] REQ-3: The full JSON export emits the same four resolution fields as the tree output; the parent-and-cluster-only partial shape no longer exists.
- [hard] REQ-4: The scoped-export caveat (a scoped node's parent may lie outside the emitted subtree, `commands/graph.rs:246-252`) is documented in the CLI reference for both export and tree surfaces.

## Notes

Keep the response envelope conventions (`{"count": N, "<collection>": [...]}` for lists). The server links the jit library directly, so this is a matter of calling the existing resolver in the route handler, not new resolution code.
